program_name: Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). The admission information states verbatim: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English.' Weighting in practice (unibz 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' listing for academic year 2026/27, both semesters): approximately 11 courses in English, 4 in Italian, 5 in German, plus one 12 CP module split IT+DE (Materials Science and Technology in IT, Mechanics of Structures in DE). English is therefore the single largest language (~55-60% of listed lectures), but several compulsory core courses are offered in one language only and have no English alternative: Mathematical Analysis 1 and Mathematical Analysis 2 (Italian), General and Inorganic Chemistry, Production Systems and Industrial Logistics, Fluid Mechanics and PLM Product Life Cycle Management (German). Consequently the programme cannot be completed in English alone. [uncertain]
campus: NOI Techpark, Bozen-Bolzano (Faculty of Engineering, Bruno-Buozzi-Strasse 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano). Single campus; no Brixen/Bruneck/Trento/Innsbruck component. Dual-study students additionally spend four of eight semesters at their partner company, which is normally located in South Tyrol.
degree_class: L-9 (Ingegneria industriale / Industrial Engineering). 180 ECTS, 3 years for the full-time study plan; 240 ECTS-equivalent over 4 years for the dual study plan.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes - actively offered and recruiting for 2026/27. All three EU application sessions (Early Bird, Late, Additional) plus the non-EU session were opened, and signed ranking lists for both the Early Bird and Late sessions of 2026/27 have already been published (50 admitted in Early Bird, 27 admitted in Late). The admission information PDF is dated 'Latest update: 29.07.2026'. Not suspended, unlike Wood Technology / Tourism Management.
is_new_programme: No - this is a long-established programme, not a first-intake programme. A published Study Manifesto exists from 2019 (Manifesto-2019-06-26-Bachelor-Industrial-Mechanical-Engineering-L9) and the AlmaLaurea transparency code for the course (0210106200900001) points to a 2009 activation cohort. The only element that is new in 2026/27 is the admission route: the ranking-list decree states that 'From the academic year 2026/2027 the possibility is introduced to use, in addition to the unibz entrance test, also the national TOLC-I/CENT-S test.' Exact first intake year not confirmed on an official 2026/27 page. [uncertain]
majors_tracks_study_plans: Four majors, each available in two study plan types. Majors: (1) Mechanics, (2) Energy, (3) Management, (4) Industrial Automation. Study plan types: (a) study plan for full-time students - 3 years / 180 ECTS; (b) dual study plan for 'working students' - 4 years, four semesters at the university and four semesters at a partner company, run with Assoimprenditori Alto Adige (association of local entrepreneurs). Brochure verbatim: 'There are two study plan types for all four majors: study plan for full-time students (3 years), dual study plan (4 years).' The first year and a half is almost identical across the four majors (mathematics, physics, materials science); specialisation follows. Mechanics, Energy and Industrial Automation are propaedeutic (feeding the Master in Industrial Mechanical Engineering and the Master in Energy Engineering); Management is more practice-oriented. Dual study is conditional: 'The dual study programmes are offered under condition of minimum 10 enrolled students. If this minimum number of students is not reached, the enrolled students can request the refund of the registration fee or they have the possibility to switch to the full-time programmes.' In the dual variant the first year is full-time; from year two work and study alternate, and the student signs an employment contract with a participating company (many belong to the Automotive Excellence Suedtirol network) at the end of year one. Only four separate study-plan web pages exist (study-plan-major-mechanics, -energy, -management, -industrial-automation); the research outline's mention of '5 study plans' could not be reproduced. [uncertain]
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed. A candidate who knows only English cannot be admitted: the entry requirement is B2 in the FIRST language and B2 in the SECOND language, where the languages are drawn from German, Italian and English. English alone satisfies only the first-language slot, so a second B2 in German or Italian is mandatory (B1 German or Italian if applying to a dual-study major). Candidates who cannot prove it are excluded before the entrance exam is even scored: 'If you do not prove the language skills required for access, you are excluded from the admission procedure.' The 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list is a hard empirical confirmation - all 7 non-EU applicants living abroad were listed under 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements required for access and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure', so the 4 non-EU places were effectively not taken up through that route; a further 13 EU-track candidates were excluded on the same ground. Even after admission the curriculum is not English-only (compulsory Italian- and German-taught core courses), and graduation demands C1/C1/B2 across all three languages. Turkish applicants with English only should treat this programme as closed unless they already hold, or can obtain before the application deadline, a recognised B2 in German or Italian.
admission_type: restricted access (numerus clausus) + entrance exam. Fixed places: 70 for EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment (50 Early Bird + 20 Late) and 4 for non-EU citizens living abroad. Selection is by a multiple-choice knowledge test in mathematics and physics/chemistry, taken as ONE of three alternatives: the unibz admission exam (online), TOLC-I, or CENT-S. A language-requirement check acts as a pre-filter before ranking. No interview, no portfolio, no motivation letter, no SAT. Ranking is by normalised test score only.
academic_requirements: Secondary school leaving certificate from the Italian system, or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. Verbatim: 'Foreign school leaving certificates are considered equivalent if obtained after 12 years of education. In this case, you furthermore must have attended at least the last two years in the foreign school system (e.g. Irish Leaving Certificate: it is not enough to attend one year and obtain the foreign certificate).' The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research imposes extra requirements on holders of certain certificates (explicitly named: American high school diplomas, British and Greek certificates) - candidates must contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). Applicants must also satisfy the language requirements or they are excluded from the procedure. No ECTS/SSD credit prerequisites apply (that regime concerns master programmes; the 2024 SSD reform codes such as IINF-04/A, MATH-03/A, IIND-07/B appear only as course classifications inside this bachelor). National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is allowed, provided they are not in the same degree class (e.g. not L-18/L-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of the course contents. A Turkish 'Lise Diplomasi' meets the 12-year rule but must be accompanied by ARDI/CIMEA documentation (see credential_recognition).
entry_exam_or_test: Three alternative tests, each with its own calendar - the applicant chooses one. (1) unibz admission exam - held ONLINE by unibz. Dates 2026/27: Early Bird 2026-05-14 at 15:00 local time; Late 2026-07-16 at 15:00; Additional Session 2026-09-14 at 15:00. Sections scored: mathematics and physics/chemistry. Preparation material published by the Faculty of Engineering: Mock Admission Test (https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Engineering/Mock-Admission-Test-ENG.pdf) and Possible Topics (https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Faculty-Engineering/Topics-Admission-ENG.pdf). (2) TOLC-I (CISIA national engineering test) - 'can be taken at any university; at unibz it will be held in person on the dates listed in the Deadlines and Important Dates section.' Sections scored for this ranking: mathematics and science. Calendar: https://testcisia.it/calendario.php?tolc=ingegneria. (3) CENT-S (CISIA) - same rules as TOLC-I; sections scored: mathematics and physics. Calendar: https://testcisia.it/calendario.php?tolc=cents&l=it&lingua=inglese. The TOLC-I/CENT-S route is newly admitted from 2026/27. No separate deadline is published for TOLC-I/CENT-S beyond 'available deadlines' on the CISIA calendar; in practice the result must exist by the application deadline of the chosen session. [uncertain]
selection_scoring: Raw scoring of the multiple-choice test (identical wording for all three test routes): '1 point for each correct answer, 0 points for each unanswered question, -0.25 points for each wrong answer.' The ranking is then built on the score 'appropriately normalized to the maximum score of each test', counting only these sections: unibz exam = mathematics and physics/chemistry; TOLC-I = mathematics and science; CENT-S = mathematics and physics. Tie-break: 'In case of equal score, priority is given to the youngest person.' No minimum pass mark / cut-off score is published for this programme - the only score-linked consequence is the OFA trigger at 30% (see ofa_rules), and admission is decided purely by rank against the available places. No grade-point-average requirement (that regime applies to master programmes such as Software Engineering 24/30 or Energy Engineering 22/30). Competition level in 2026/27 was low: Early Bird produced exactly 50 admitted plus a single waiting-list candidate at position 51, and the Late session admitted 27; the real filter was the language requirement, not the test score. Absence of a published threshold is inferred from the ranking-list decree and the admission PDF, neither of which mentions one. [uncertain]
bonus_points: None. No Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Master in Accounting and Finance), no start-up project bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation). The ranking depends exclusively on the normalised admission-test score, with age as the sole tie-breaker.
portfolio_and_materials: None required. No portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no motivation letter and no CV are requested for this programme - unlike Design and Art, Critical Creative Practices or Eco-Social Design. The only uploads are the identity document, the school leaving certificate/diploma, language certificates and (for foreign qualifications) the ARDI/CIMEA statements. Format limits published for other unibz programmes (portfolio max 20 MB PDF, project proposal max 2 A4, motivation letter max 6,000 characters, video max 2 minutes) do not apply here.
interview: No interview. Selection is fully test-based; the Admission Committee (chaired within the Faculty of Engineering, members include Prof. Alessandro Artale and Prof. Giovanni Modanese in the 2026/27 decree) only evaluates documents uploaded to the portal by the application deadline plus the admission-test score. No interview dates are published for this programme.
conditional_admission: Applicants who have not yet obtained their secondary school diploma may apply: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.' Until the required foreign-qualification documents are uploaded, admission is 'only with reservation' (ammesso con riserva); if the qualification is later judged unsuitable the candidate is excluded, and exclusion by Rector's decree remains possible even after enrolment. Financial protection: the first instalment is refunded only if the candidate fails the secondary school final exam, or - for non-EU applicants living abroad - does not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities. There is NO ECTS-based conditional admission (the 120/140 ECTS rule in the field definition applies to master programmes), and no late-enrolment window to 11/12/2026 is published for this bachelor. [uncertain]
ofa_rules: OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) applies. Verbatim: 'If the applicant obtains a percentage less than or equal to 30% of the maximum achievable score in the relevant sections of the admission exam, they will be assigned additional learning requirements (OFA) to be fulfilled during the first year of the programme.' A preparatory course is organised in the weeks before the first semester (mathematics pre-course 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-09) so students can sit the OFA remedial test. 'The OFA test must be passed within the first academic year and is an essential requirement for taking curricular exams in the following years. If the applicant does not pass the OFA test, they will not be allowed to take the exams scheduled for the second and third year of the programme.' Note this is a mathematics/physics OFA tied to the entrance test, not the mandatory-maths-test OFA used by Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics or Tourism Sport and Event Management.
language_requirements: Trilingual regime with a hard two-language entry bar. Entry: B2 in the first language AND B2 in the second language (dual-study majors: B2 first language, B1 second language); no level required in the third language at entry. The three languages are German, Italian and English - 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (B2 or C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' Failure to prove the required levels means exclusion from the admission procedure ('otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure'). Certification is mandatory for the first and second language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the third. B1 in the third language is the minimum for sitting curricular exams held in that language; if the first semester is taught only in English and English is the applicant's third language, at least B1 English must be certified by mid-January. Exit (to graduate): C1 first language, C1 second language, B2 third language. CEFR levels apply throughout. Free Language Centre courses support the third language (target B1 by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2). For an English-only international applicant this is the binding constraint - see english_only_accessibility.
entry_levels_by_position: Levels are defined by POSITION, not by which language it is. Standard (full-time) study plans: 1st language B2 / 2nd language B2 / 3rd language no level required. Dual study majors: 1st language B2 / 2nd language B1 / 3rd language no level required. A B1 in the third language is required in order to sit curricular examinations taught in that language (and must be certified by mid-January of year 1 if English is the third language and semester 1 is English-only). The applicant chooses which of German/Italian/English occupies each position, based on the levels actually certified; the first language is the strongest. Compared with sister programmes at the same faculty: Computer Science B2/B2/none, Electronic and Information Engineering B2/B1/none - Industrial and Mechanical Engineering sits at the stricter B2/B2 for the full-time plans and relaxes to B2/B1 only for dual study.
exit_levels: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2. These are graduation requirements, not admission requirements, and directly gate the degree: a student admitted at B2/B2 must raise both to C1 and reach B2 in the third language before graduating. The Language Centre offers the courses free of charge and sets intermediate milestones for the third language (B1 by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2). The programme also carries a 3 CP 'Specialized Language' course in every major's study plan.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the threshold for taking curricular examinations delivered in that language. Verbatim: 'A B1 level in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that specific language.' Special case: 'if the first semester of your study programme is only taught in English and your third language is English, you will have to certify at least a B1 level in English by mid-January to be able to take all the curricular exams scheduled for the first semester.' Students without a third-language certificate sit a placement test after admission and are assigned a learning path; absolute beginners must use the September intensive course because A1 beginner courses are offered exclusively in the September pre-semester session and no longer during the academic year.
proof_pathways: Four accepted routes to prove language proficiency. (1) The main teaching language of the final high school year, if German, Italian or English - recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian). For foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter from the school stating it must also be uploaded. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English - recognised as C1; foreign degrees again need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if not on the diploma. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list (https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf); if it cannot be uploaded it may be e-mailed as PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) A language exam organised by the unibz Language Centre, booked online through the application portal ('enrol for language exams') after creating the application - note 'you can only register for B2 level exams.' 2026/27 online language exam dates and registration windows: 2026-03-16 (registration 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09); 2026-04-16, 2026-04-17, 2026-04-20 and 2026-04-21 (registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08); 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26 for the Late session (registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15). If the application is started outside a registration window the applicant must return to the portal during one of these windows. Additional route for bilingual/multilingual and foreign secondary schools: if CEFR levels for German, Italian or English are explicitly printed on the leaving certificate and all four skills were assessed, those levels are accepted for the second and/or third language, subject to Language Centre approval. Certificates from Italian public institutions require a self-declaration; those from foreign public institutions require a scanned copy of the original.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council n. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants'). Rules, verbatim from the English section: a certificate must 'include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself' and must 'indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade'. 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed.' 'There is no compensation for failed parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.' 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam (home edition) are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list.' Certificates covering single skills from different organisations are refused; certificates of participation, end-of-course tests, private-institution exams and placement-test results are refused; certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff are refused; 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.' Validity: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January' (i.e. certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth year preceding submission remain valid for the whole of that year). Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Recognised providers include Goethe-Institut and OeSD for German, and the corresponding boards for Italian and English, level by level A2-C2.
application_deadline_eu: Three separate sessions for EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment; all cut-offs are at 12:00 noon local time. (1) Early Bird Application: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. (2) Late Application (EU only): 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. (3) Additional Application Session (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September only if places remain): 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. Original unibz notation, DD/MM/YYYY: '02/03 - 28/04/2026', '28/05 - 08/07/2026', '18/08 - 04/09/2026'. Candidates excluded in the first session may reapply in the next one, and a test score already obtained remains valid for a re-application in the second session. Once submitted, an application cannot be modified.
application_deadline_non_eu: One single window for non-EU citizens living abroad: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28 (12:00 noon local time) - i.e. the Early Bird session only. Verbatim: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are excluded from the Late Application and from the Additional Application Session, both of which are explicitly EU-only. A non-refundable EUR 50 application fee applies to this group. Practical consequence for Turkish applicants resident in Turkey: the 2026-04-28 noon deadline is the only chance in the cycle, and the required B2+B2 language proof must already be in hand or booked via a Language Centre exam on 2026-03-16 or 2026-04-16/17/20/21.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU citizens. (1) 'Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State'. (2) 'Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: permesso di soggiorno for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not sufficient. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.' Critical warning: 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' This third category is the decisive one for Turkish nationals already living in Italy on a work, family or humanitarian permit - it grants access to the 70-place EU pool, both the Early Bird and Late sessions and the Additional Session, and removes the EUR 50 application fee and the Universitaly/visa route.
places_quotas: EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment: 50 places in the Early Bird Application + 20 places in the Late Application = 70 total (the brochure states 'Places available: 70 EU + 4 Non-EU'). Non-EU citizens living abroad: 4 places, Early Bird only. Additional Application Session: no separate quota - it is opened only 'if there are available places'. Any places left unfilled in the Early Bird round are rolled into the Late Application: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application.' 2026/27 outcome: 50 admitted in Early Bird with only one candidate on the waiting list at position 51, and 27 admitted in the Late session (more than the nominal 20, confirming that unclaimed early-bird places rolled over); all 7 non-EU applicants living abroad were excluded on language grounds, so the 4 non-EU places were not awarded through that route.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: Early Bird: ranking list published by 2026-05-27; first instalment of tuition fees (EUR 600, secures the place) by 2026-06-05 12:00 noon; online enrolment 2026-07-10 to 2026-08-06 12:00 noon; waiting-list candidates contacted by e-mail from 2026-06-08. Late Application: ranking by 2026-07-30; first instalment by 2026-08-06 12:00 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-08-06 12:00 noon. Additional Session: ranking by 2026-09-18; first instalment by 2026-09-25 12:00 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 2026-09-25 12:00 noon. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic loss of the place, which passes to the next candidate in the ranking. A candidate admitted to more than one programme may secure a maximum of 2 programmes by paying the instalment twice. Paying does not confer student status - only enrolment does - and payments are non-refundable except for failure of the secondary school final exam or, for non-EU applicants abroad, failure to obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities. Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Administrative Court of Bozen within 60 days of publication.
programme_specific_dates: unibz admission exam (online), programme-specific: 2026-05-14 at 15:00 (Early Bird), 2026-07-16 at 15:00 (Late), 2026-09-14 at 15:00 (Additional Session), all local time. TOLC-I / CENT-S: taken on CISIA calendar dates at any university; at unibz held in person on the same session dates. Language exams (online, Language Centre): 2026-03-16 (registration 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09); 2026-04-16, 2026-04-17, 2026-04-20, 2026-04-21 (registration 2026-03-24 to 2026-04-08); 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-26 (registration 2026-05-28 to 2026-06-15). Preparatory phase 2026/27: intensive language courses 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-18 (Monday to Friday, 6 h/day); mathematics pre-course (also the OFA preparation) 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-09; Freshers Days 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29. Academic calendar: 1st semester classes 2026-09-28 to 2026-12-23, holidays 2026-12-24 to 2027-01-06, classes resume 2027-01-07 to 2027-01-23, exams 2027-01-25 to 2027-02-20; 2nd semester classes 2027-03-01 to 2027-03-25, holidays 2027-03-26 to 2027-03-29, classes 2027-03-30 to 2027-06-12, exams 2027-06-14 to 2027-07-10; autumn exam session 2027-08-23 to 2027-09-25. Third-language B1 certification deadline for English-only first semesters: mid-January. Dual study: employment contract with a partner company signed at the end of year 1; the dual plan runs only if at least 10 students enrol.
required_documents: At application: (a) an account on the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup) plus a valid ID card or passport, front and back, scanned - 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (b) the completed online form with all attachments; (c) the secondary school leaving certificate / diploma - if the qualification was gained abroad and the diploma is not yet issued, it must be uploaded at enrolment instead; (d) language proof - self-declaration if the certificate was awarded by an Italian public institution, scanned copy of the original if awarded by a foreign public institution, plus (where relevant) a school or university letter stating the medium of instruction; (e) for parity-of-treatment applicants, a copy of the valid Italian permit to stay (or renewal request). At enrolment, for foreign secondary school qualifications: the secondary school diploma; an official translation into Italian (not required for diplomas issued in German or English); and, depending on the education system, the ARDI Statement of Correspondence and/or the CIMEA Statements (see credential_recognition). No structured study-career Excel template is required for this bachelor (that upload belongs to master applications). Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Applications cannot be modified after submission, and only documents uploaded by the deadline are evaluated.
application_fee: EUR 50, charged only to non-EU citizens living abroad. Verbatim: 'Application fee: EUR 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.' EU citizens and persons given parity of treatment (including non-EU nationals holding an Italian work/family/humanitarian/religious residence permit) pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Approximately EUR 1,200 per academic year, in two instalments: 1st instalment EUR 600 (includes the EUR 16 revenue stamp / marca da bollo), paid to secure the place after the ranking list; 2nd instalment EUR 600, due by March of the following year. Late payment of the second instalment incurs a fine; unpaid fees block exams and any transfer to another university or programme. No refund on drop-out, interruption or exclusion. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (certificate to be handed in at the start of the academic year); foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship. Students holding a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano receive a refund of the tuition fees. Fee pages: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/studying-at-unibz
scholarships_grants: Main instrument is the provincial study grant of the Autonomous Province of South Tyrol, administered by the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario / Amt fuer Hochschulfoerderung, awarded on income and merit; unibz communicates a range of roughly EUR 1,680 to EUR 6,960 per year, and grant holders additionally receive a refund of their tuition fees. Three provincial instruments exist: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships and postgraduate study grants; applications are filed through the province's e-government portal, with help available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. Decisive restriction for international applicants: non-EU students qualify only if they hold a long-term residence permit or 'after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' - so a first-year non-EU student arriving on a study visa is effectively excluded in year one. Exemption from tuition fees applies to holders of an Italian government scholarship and to students with the recognised disability status described above. Other sources referenced by unibz: German BAfoeG, Austrian and Italian government grants. No scholarship specific to the Bachelor in Industrial and Mechanical Engineering is published; dual-study students are instead paid by their partner company under an employment contract. The EUR 1,680-6,960 range and the 27/30 merit-average rule mentioned in the field definition were not re-confirmed on a 2026/27 unibz page during this verification. [uncertain]
credential_recognition: For a foreign secondary school qualification, upload at enrolment: the diploma itself plus an official Italian translation (not needed for diplomas issued in German or English), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate - the Statement of Correspondence downloaded from ARDI, the Automatic Recognition Database Italy (https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention - the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification; (c) non-EU countries that are not signatories to the Lisbon Convention - the CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification (https://cimea-diplome.it/). Turkey is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so a Turkish applicant falls in category (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification, and no Italian translation is needed only if the diploma is issued in German or English (a Turkish-language diploma therefore does require an official Italian translation). Until these documents are uploaded the candidate can be admitted 'only with reservation'; unibz performs its own checks, may request further documents, and can exclude a student by Rector's decree even after enrolment if the qualification proves invalid. The 180-ECTS evidence requirement mentioned in the field definition applies to master admission and not to this bachelor.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply in the single Early Bird window with the EUR 50 fee; if admitted per the ranking list, secure the place by paying the first instalment (EUR 600) by 2026-06-05 noon; then start the visa application on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/) - 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The Italian diplomatic-consular representation in the applicant's country then issues the study visa; unibz stresses that 'the admission to unibz does not confer automatically any right to obtaining a visa' and that the university application 'does not guarantee an appointment at the diplomatic-consular Italian representation'. Proof of financial means: roughly EUR 800 per month of living costs in Bozen-Bolzano excluding tuition, which unibz translates into a minimum of about EUR 36,000 for a bachelor programme (EUR 24,000 for a master), plus health insurance and visa expenses and the approximately EUR 1,200 annual tuition. After arrival: 'within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, you must have applied for the residence permit' - contact the Advisory Service on arrival, and hand the permesso di soggiorno to the Student Office in person or by e-mail once obtained. Work while studying: with a study residence permit, part-time work of no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Scholarship caveat: provincial grants require a long-term permit or one uninterrupted year of registered residence in South Tyrol. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who cannot obtain the enrolment documents from the Italian authorities are entitled to a refund of the instalment paid.

uncertainty_notes: 1) Academic year: all dates, quotas and fees are the published 2026/27 cycle. As of the verification date (2026-08-29) that cycle is essentially closed - the Early Bird and Late ranking lists are already signed and published, and only the Additional Session (application 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04) may still be running; figures for 2027/28 are not yet published. 2) Study plan count: the research outline notes '5 study plans' for this programme, but only four study-plan pages exist (Mechanics, Energy, Management, Industrial Automation) and unibz describes 'two study plan types for all four majors', i.e. 8 major/plan combinations rather than 5. The discrepancy could not be resolved from official pages. 3) Teaching-language weighting: the 11 EN / 4 IT / 5 DE split comes from the 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' page, which unibz explicitly says 'shows the lectures that are currently offered in the two semesters. It does not illustrate the structure of the study programme' - it is therefore a snapshot, not a full-curriculum count, and language allocation can change by cohort and major. 4) Dual study: it is stated that dual plans exist for all four majors, but no separate dual study plan page or dual-specific curriculum is published in English, and the dual page is written for companies rather than applicants; the list of participating companies and how an international applicant would secure a contract are not published. 5) TOLC-I / CENT-S: no explicit cut-off date is given for taking the national test - the programme page only links the CISIA calendars, so the assumption that the result must exist by the session's application deadline is an inference. 6) Selection threshold: no minimum pass mark is published anywhere for this programme; the absence is inferred from the admission PDF and the signed ranking decree. 7) Scholarship amounts: the EUR 1,680-6,960 provincial grant range and the post-first-year merit average were not re-confirmed on a current unibz page during this verification; the unibz Study Guide page names the grant types but not the amounts. 8) Official call: unibz publishes no English-language bando for bachelor programmes; the Admission Regulations referenced in the ranking decree are available only in Italian and German. 9) Programme regulations (Regolamento didattico) are likewise published in Italian and German only. 10) The admission-information PDF slug differs from the page URL ('bachelor-in-industrial-and-mechanical-engineering' vs 'bachelor-industrial-mechanical-engineering'); a scraper using the page slug will get a 404. 11) Non-EU reality check: in 2026/27 every single non-EU applicant living abroad was rejected for failing the two-language B2 requirement, so the nominal 4 non-EU places should not be read as 4 realistic openings for English-only candidates.
